charts.title: 01_baseline_parity
charts.caption: At-rest baseline (no infection): the real BioGears 8.2.0 engine and the SBML extraction settle to the same StandardMale haemodynamics — SBP 114.9 vs 114.6 mmHg, DBP 74.5 vs 73.5, HR 72.2 vs 71.5 /min, cardiac output 5.81 vs 5.9 L/min — all within ~1 mmHg / ~0.7 bpm / ~0.1 L/min of each other and of the StandardMale target (y-axes zoomed to the target band so the small differences are visible). This is the parity gate: because both sides start from the same state, the divergence measured under infection in studies 02-03 is attributable to the model, not a mismatched starting point. Values are the committed severity-0 run results (engine 5 min, SBML 30 s).

charts.title: Functional-difference matrix — divergence mapped to omitted subsystems
charts.caption: Map of BioGears functionality to its fate in the extraction and to the run-for-run result. The inflammation core is translated faithfully (identical output); the cardiovascular control and fluid systems are simplified; and a cluster of vasomotor/fluid/metabolic subsystems (nitric oxide, fever vasodilation, renal/urine, lactate, intracellular water, respiration, nutrition) is omitted or inert — exactly the pathways that would couple into SVR, CO and volume, which is where every divergence lands.

charts.title: Event-free proto_valve vs full model (same engine) — tracks to <0.7 mmHg / ~1e-9, at ~6% on CO/SVR
charts.caption: Event-free proto_valve vs the full event-driven sepsis_sbml model, both run through the same roadrunner/CVODE engine and the same Composite harness (severity 3, 2 h). Removing E_beat and the piecewise pulOpen valve leaves the filtered hemodynamics and the immune core almost unchanged: MAP tracks within 0.56 mmHg, HR within 0.098 /min, and blood pathogen / tissue integrity agree to 1e-09 relative. Cardiac output and SVR differ most (~6% / ~6%) because the 5 s filters and the continuous beat phase replace the per-beat latched values — instantaneous points are not meant to line up (compare per-beat summaries). This is the fidelity cost of the event-free speedup, measured within one engine so it isolates the structural change from the engine-vs-engine divergence that is the rest of this study.
